title: Success is an artifact on disk, not an exit code or a self-report
statement: Decide whether a stage succeeded by checking for a concrete artifact it was required to produce, never by trusting its exit code or the agent's own claim of success.
rationale: Agents and shells both report success unreliably; a stage can exit zero having produced nothing. An artifact that must exist is a fact the harness can check independently of anything the agent says.
applies_when: Stages run unattended under time limits
not_when: A human is watching every stage and can judge output directly
how: Define each stage's required output file up front
Treat the stage as failed unless that file exists and is non-empty
Never call a timeout a failure without first checking whether the output file exists
check: Does the orchestrator gate on os.path.exists of a declared artifact rather than on the return code? If it reads exit codes or parses agent prose, it is trusting the wrong signal.
failure_if_absent: Empty or partial work is recorded as shipped, and a killed-but-complete stage is wrongly discarded.

evidence.title: agent-failure-modes INC-0006 - checkpoint-first
evidence.quote: Success is an ARTIFACT, not an exit code. Under a hard timeout, an agent that writes its minimal complete output first and refines in place still succeeds if killed.
evidence.note: First-party corpus of loop failures; this rule is derived from a specific incident.
